title: Changes in the morphology and function of the sub-basal corneal nerve plexus after accelerated corneal cross-linking: A one-year follow-up study

groups.description: 47 eyes of 34 patients with progressive keratoconus (inclusion: older than 14 years, thinnest pachymetry at least 375 µm; pellucid marginal degeneration excluded) treated with epithelium-off accelerated cross-linking, 9-mm epithelial removal, riboflavin for 20 minutes, 30 mW/cm2 for 4 minutes (7.2 J/cm2, KXL I); single centre, examined preoperatively and at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months

series.notes: values printed as 'x ± y' without a stated statistic; the leading number is taken as the group mean; Kmax defined as 'Steepest keratometric' in the table footnote, unit D in the row label; 43 eyes of 31 patients returned at 1 year (ordinary attrition) and the article does not state whether the pre-op mean covers all 47 eyes or only the eyes seen at 1 year; device from the Methods: Pentacam Scheimpflug tomographer (Oculus)

exclusions.reason: p-values are not admissible as values

notes: Single-arm study of a standard accelerated protocol (no investigational agent declared), so the group is a control
Patients were to be followed for at least 1 year, but fewer eyes returned at each visit (35, 33, 42 and 43 eyes at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months), so the group is not a complete-case subset
Age: inclusion older than 14 years with mean ± SD only and no range; neither 'all older than 18' nor 'some 18 or younger' can be established, so the age group is unstated
Table 2 also gives K1, K2 and thinnest corneal thickness: other keratometry and thickness, not extracted
Table 3 (corneal sensitivity), Table 4 (sub-basal nerve plexus) and Table 5 (literature summary): not extracted
